examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.
You look like some rich crook.
He is a very rich man.

examples.text: Не верю. Похож на какого-то богатого ворюгу.
examples.trans: I don't buy it. You look like some rich crook.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)
+ dative of person + accusative of thing
imperative давай/давайте + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

related.gloss: to hand in; to take (an exam)

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: забирать деньги = to take the money
забирать детей из школы = to pick the kids up from school

examples.trans: I pick the children up from school.

examples.text: А я тебе делаю условный срок. Плюс ты забираешь все деньги Вики.
examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.
In the kitchen they are preparing this order.
Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.en: to lend (colloquial with dative: займите мне денег)

examples.trans: Then lend me at least some money.

examples.text: Ладно, ну займите тогда хотя бы денег.
examples.trans: Fine, then lend me at least some money.
Who took first place after all?

meanings.note: To run for a second term.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Как вы знаете = as you know.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?
All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.
I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.
Yulia, bring a pen and a piece of paper.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Used as an exclamation of approval.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.en: match (in a relationship: я не пара вам = I'm no match for you)

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you.
They are a very handsome couple.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам. Вы красавец, а я старая.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you. You're a handsome man, and I'm old.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Let us talk a bit later.
Let us go to the cinema a bit later.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!
The guest at table five is waiting.
Who is sitting at the fifth table?
Nastya, quickly clear the fifth table!

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Секунду! = One second! / Just a moment!

examples.trans: One second. I'll call right now.
One second. I'll call Mishkin right now.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: plural only; declines like an adjective: чаевых, чаевым
the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
